sanskrit: narāntakaṃ hataṃ dṛṣṭvā cukruśur nairṛtarṣabhāḥ devāntakas trimūrdhā ca paulastyaś ca mahodaraḥ
english: Seeing Narāntaka slain, the bull-chiefs among the Rākṣasas cried out — Devāntaka, Triśiras, and Mahodara, descendant of Pulastya.

sanskrit: ārūḍho meghasaṃkāśaṃ vāraṇendraṃ mahodaraḥ vāliputraṃ mahāvīryam abhidudrāva vīryavān
english: Mahodara, mighty in valour, mounted upon an elephant lord resembling a thundercloud and charged at Aṅgada, son of Vālin, of great heroic power.

sanskrit: bhrātṛvyasanasaṃtaptas tadā devāntako balī ādāya parighaṃ dīptam aṅgadaṃ samabhidravat
english: Devāntaka, the powerful one, scorched by grief at his kinsman's misfortune, took up a blazing iron club and rushed at Aṅgada.

sanskrit: ratham ādityasaṃkāśaṃ yuktaṃ paramavājibhiḥ āsthāya triśirā vīro vāliputram athābhyayāt
english: Triśiras the hero, mounting a chariot bright as the sun and yoked with the finest horses, then advanced against the son of Vālin.

sanskrit: sa tribhir devadarpaghnair nairṛtendrair abhidrutaḥ vṛkṣam utpāṭayām āsa mahāviṭapam aṅgadaḥ
english: Assailed simultaneously by those three lord-Rākṣasas who crush the pride of the gods, Aṅgada uprooted a great tree with massive branches.

sanskrit: devāntakāya taṃ vīraś cikṣepa sahasāṅgadaḥ mahāvṛkṣaṃ mahāśākhaṃ śakro dīptam ivāśanim
english: That hero Aṅgada hurled that enormous tree with its great boughs at Devāntaka swiftly, like Indra hurling a blazing thunderbolt.

sanskrit: triśirās taṃ praciccheda śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ sa vṛkṣaṃ kṛttam ālokya utpapāta tato 'ṅgadaḥ
english: Triśiras cut that tree to pieces with arrows like venomous serpents. Seeing the tree severed, Aṅgada then leapt up.

sanskrit: sa vavarṣa tato vṛkṣāñ śilāś ca kapikuñjaraḥ tān praciccheda saṃkruddhas triśirā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then that bull among monkeys showered trees and rocks upon them; Triśiras, filled with rage, cut them all down with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: parighāgreṇa tān vṛkṣān babhañja ca surāntakaḥ triśirāś cāṅgadaṃ vīram abhidudrāva sāyakaiḥ
english: Devāntaka also shattered those trees with the tip of his club, and Triśiras charged at the hero Aṅgada with arrows.

sanskrit: gajena samabhidrutya vāliputraṃ mahodaraḥ jaghānorasi saṃkruddhas tomarair vajrasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: Mahodara, mounted on his elephant, charged at the son of Vālin in rage and struck him on the chest with javelins like thunderbolts.

sanskrit: devāntakaś ca saṃkruddhaḥ parigheṇa tadāṅgadam upagamyābhihatyāśu vyapacakrāma vegavān
english: Devāntaka too, filled with fury, swiftly approached Aṅgada, struck him hard with his club, and then withdrew with speed.

sanskrit: sa tribhir nairṛtaśreṣṭhair yugapat samabhidrutaḥ na vivyathe mahātejā vāliputraḥ pratāpavān
english: Assailed simultaneously by those three foremost Rākṣasas, the great-spirited, illustrious son of Vālin did not waver.

sanskrit: talena bhṛśam utpatya jaghānāsya mahāgajam petatur locane tasya vinanāda sa vāraṇaḥ
english: Leaping up forcefully, he struck the great elephant with his palm; the beast's eyes fell out and it trumpeted in agony.

sanskrit: viṣāṇaṃ cāsya niṣkṛṣya vāliputro mahābalaḥ devāntakam abhidrutya tāḍayām āsa saṃyuge
english: The mighty son of Vālin then wrenched out its tusk and, charging at Devāntaka, struck him in battle.

sanskrit: sa vihvalitasarvāṅgo vātoddhata iva drumaḥ lākṣārasasavarṇaṃ ca susrāva rudhiraṃ mukhāt
english: He, his entire body staggered like a tree shaken by the wind, poured blood from his mouth the colour of lac-juice.

sanskrit: athāśvāsya mahātejāḥ kṛcchrād devāntako balī āvidhya parighaṃ ghoraṃ ājaghāna tadāṅgadam
english: Then the mighty Devāntaka, recovering with great difficulty from that blow, whirled his terrible club and struck Aṅgada.

sanskrit: parighābhihataś cāpi vānarendrātmajas tadā jānubhyāṃ patito bhūmau punar evotpapāta ha
english: Struck by the club, the son of the lord of monkeys fell to the ground on his knees, but sprang up again at once.

sanskrit: samutpatantaṃ triśirās tribhir āśīviṣopamaiḥ ghorair haripateḥ putraṃ lalāṭe 'bhijaghāna ha
english: As he leapt up, Triśiras struck the son of the lord of monkeys on the forehead with three terrible arrows like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: tato 'ṅgadaṃ parikṣiptaṃ tribhir nairṛtapuṃgavaiḥ hanūmān api vijñāya nīlaś cāpi pratasthatuḥ
english: Then Hanūmān and Nīla, perceiving that Aṅgada was being overwhelmed by those three bull-Rākṣasas, advanced to help.

sanskrit: tataś cikṣepa śailāgraṃ nīlas triśirase tadā tad rāvaṇasuto dhīmān bibheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Nīla hurled a mountain peak at Triśiras; but that wise son of Rāvaṇa shattered it with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tad bāṇaśatanirbhinnaṃ vidāritaśilātalam savisphuliṅgaṃ sajvālaṃ nipapāta gireḥ śiraḥ
english: The peak of the mountain, pierced by hundreds of arrows, its stony surface split asunder, with sparks and flames, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tato jṛmbhitam ālokya harṣād devāntakas tadā parigheṇābhidudrāva mārutātmajam āhave
english: Then Devāntaka, seeing that gap in the attack, charged joyfully with his iron club at the son of the Wind in battle.

sanskrit: tam āpatantam utpatya hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ ājaghāna tadā mūrdhni vajravegena muṣṭinā
english: Leaping to meet his charge, Hanūmān son of the Wind struck him then on the crown of his head with a fist of thunderbolt force.

sanskrit: sa muṣṭiniṣpiṣṭavikīrṇamūrdhā nirvāntadantākṣivilambijihvaḥ devāntako rākṣasarājasūnur gatāsur urvyāṃ sahasā papāta
english: His skull crushed and shattered by that fist, his teeth, eyes, and tongue dangling out, Devāntaka, son of the king of Rākṣasas, fell to the earth lifeless at once.

sanskrit: tasmin hate rākṣasayodhamukhye mahābale saṃyati devaśatrau kruddhas trimūrdhā niśitāgram ugraṃ vavarṣa nīlorasi bāṇavarṣam
english: When that foremost Rākṣasa warrior, mighty and a foe of the gods, was slain in battle, Triśiras in rage showered a fierce torrent of sharp-tipped arrows upon Nīla's chest.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ śaraughair abhivarṣyamāṇo vibhinnagātraḥ kapisainyapālaḥ nīlo babhūvātha visṛṣṭagātro viṣṭambhitas tena mahābalena
english: Nīla, guardian of the monkey army, his body pierced and his limbs gone limp from those showers of arrows, was thus rendered inert by the might of that powerful one.

sanskrit: tatas tu nīlaḥ pratilabhya saṃjñāṃ śailaṃ samutpāṭya savṛkṣaṣaṇḍam tataḥ samutpatya bhṛśogravego mahodaraṃ tena jaghāna mūrdhni
english: But then Nīla, regaining his senses, uprooted a mountain with its cluster of trees, and leaping up with fierce tremendous speed, struck Mahodara on the head with it.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa śailābhinipātabhagno mahodaras tena saha dvipena vipothito bhūmitale gatāsuḥ papāta varjābhihato yathādriḥ
english: Then Mahodara, shattered by the mountain's impact and pulverised together with his elephant, fell to the ground bereft of life, like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: pitṛvyaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā triśirāś cāpam ādade hanūmantaṃ ca saṃkruddho vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Seeing his uncle slain, Triśiras took up his bow and, filled with fury, pierced Hanūmān with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: hanūmāṃs tu samutpatya hayāṃs triśirasas tadā vidadāra nakhaiḥ kruddho gajendraṃ mṛgarāḍ iva
english: But Hanūmān, springing forward in wrath, tore apart Triśiras's horses with his claws, as a lion king tears an elephant lord.

sanskrit: atha śaktiṃ samādāya kālarātrim ivāntakaḥ cikṣepānilaputrāya triśirā rāvaṇātmajaḥ
english: Then Triśiras, son of Rāvaṇa, took up a śakti-spear like the Night of Cosmic Dissolution wielded by Death itself, and hurled it at the son of the Wind.

sanskrit: divi kṣiptām ivolkāṃ tāṃ śaktiṃ kṣiptām asaṃgatām gṛhītvā hariśārdūlo babhañja ca nanāda ca
english: That śakti, hurled and still hurtling through the air like a meteor launched into the sky, was caught by that tiger among monkeys; he broke it and roared.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā ghorasaṃkāśāṃ śaktiṃ bhagnāṃ hanūmatā prahṛṣṭā vānaragaṇā vinedur jaladā iva
english: Seeing that fearsome śakti broken by Hanūmān, the monkey host exulted and shouted like thunderclouds.

sanskrit: tataḥ khaḍgaṃ samudyamya triśirā rākṣasottamaḥ nicakhāna tadā roṣād vānarendrasya vakṣasi
english: Then Triśiras, foremost among Rākṣasas, raised his sword and in fury drove it into the chest of the lord of monkeys.

sanskrit: khaḍgaprahārābhihato hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ ājaghāna trimūrdhānaṃ talenorasi vīryavān
english: Struck by the sword blow, Hanūmān son of the Wind, still mighty, struck Triśiras on the chest with his open palm.

sanskrit: sa talabhihatas tena srastahastāmbaro bhuvi nipapāta mahātejās triśirās tyaktacetanaḥ
english: Struck by that palm blow, the great-spirited Triśiras fell to the ground, his arms hanging limp, his clothing dishevelled, his senses departed.

sanskrit: sa tasya patataḥ khaḍgaṃ samācchidya mahākapiḥ nanāda girisaṃkāśas trāsayan sarvanairṛtān
english: That great monkey, mountain-like, snatched the sword from the fallen one and roared, terrifying all the Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇas taṃ ghoṣam utpapāta niśācaraḥ utpatya ca hanūmantaṃ tāḍayām āsa muṣṭinā
english: Unable to endure that roar, the night-ranger leapt up and, springing at Hanūmān, struck him with his fist.

sanskrit: tena muṣṭiprahāreṇa saṃcukopa mahākapiḥ kupitaś ca nijagrāha kirīṭe rākṣasarṣabham
english: At that fist-blow the great monkey blazed with rage, and in his fury seized that bull among Rākṣasas by his crown.

sanskrit: sa tasya śīrṣāṇy asinā śitena kirīṭajuṣṭāni sakuṇḍalāni kruddhaḥ praciccheda suto 'nilasya tvaṣṭuḥ sutasyeva śirāṃsi śakraḥ
english: With a sharp sword the son of Anila, enraged, cut off those heads adorned with crowns and earrings, just as Indra once cut off the heads of the son of Tvaṣṭṛ.

sanskrit: tāny āyatākṣāṇy agasaṃnibhāni pradīptavaiśvānaralocanāni petuḥ śirāṃsīndraripor dharaṇyāṃ jyotīṃṣi muktāni yathārkamārgāt
english: Those heads of Indra's foe fell to the earth — their elongated eyes like mountains, their pupils blazing like Vaiśvānara — like celestial lights released from the sun's path.

sanskrit: tasmin hate devaripau triśīrṣe hanūmata śakraparākrameṇa neduḥ plavaṃgāḥ pracacāla bhūmī rakṣāṃsy atho dudruvire samantāt
english: When that three-headed foe of the gods was slain by Hanūmān with the might of Indra, the monkeys shouted, the earth trembled, and the Rākṣasas fled on all sides.

sanskrit: hataṃ triśirasaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathaiva ca mahodaram hatau prekṣya durādharṣau devāntakanarāntakau
english: Seeing Triśiras slain, and likewise Mahodara, and beholding the slaughter of Devāntaka and Narāntaka — those two who were hard to assail —

sanskrit: cukopa paramāmarṣī mahāpārśvo mahābalaḥ jagrāhārciṣmatīṃ cāpi gadāṃ sarvāyasīṃ śubhām
english: the supremely wrathful Mahāpārśva, mighty in strength, blazed with anger and seized an all-iron mace, gleaming with flame.

sanskrit: hemapaṭṭaparikṣiptāṃ māṃsaśoṇitalepanām virājamānāṃ vapuṣā śatruśoṇitarañjitām
english: It was encased in bands of gold, smeared with flesh and blood, resplendent in its form, dyed with the blood of enemies.

sanskrit: tejasā saṃpradīptāgrāṃ raktamālyavibhūṣitām airāvatamahāpadmasārvabhauma bhayāvahām
english: Its tip ablaze with energy, adorned with garlands of red flowers, inspiring terror in Airāvata, Mahāpadma, and Sārvabhauma alike.

sanskrit: gadām ādāya saṃkruddho mahāpārśvo mahābalaḥ harīn samabhidudrāva yugāntāgnir iva jvalan
english: Seizing that mace and blazing with fury, the mighty Mahāpārśva rushed at the monkeys, blazing like the fire at the end of an age.

sanskrit: atharṣayaḥ samutpatya vānaro ravaṇānujam mahāpārśvam upāgamya tasthau tasyāgrato balī
english: Then that monkey Ṛṣabha, son of Varuṇa, leapt up and, approaching Rāvaṇa's brother Mahāpārśva, stood before him powerfully.

sanskrit: taṃ purastāt sthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānaraṃ parvatopamam ājaghānorasi kruddho gadayā vajrakalpayā
english: Seeing that mountain-like monkey standing before him, Mahāpārśva, enraged, struck him on the chest with his mace equal to a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sa tayābhihatas tena gadayā vānararṣabhaḥ bhinnavakṣāḥ samādhūtaḥ susrāva rudhiraṃ bahu
english: Struck by that mace, the bull among monkeys, his chest cloven and his body shaken, poured forth a great flow of blood.

sanskrit: sa saṃprāpya cirāt saṃjñām ṛṣabho vānararṣabhaḥ kruddho visphuramāṇauṣṭho mahāpārśvam udaikṣata
english: Ṛṣabha, that bull among monkeys, regaining his senses after some time, gazed at Mahāpārśva in fury with quivering lips.

sanskrit: tāṃ gṛhītvā gadāṃ bhīmām āvidhya ca punaḥ punaḥ mattānīkaṃ mahāpārśvaṃ jaghāna raṇamūrdhani
english: Seizing that terrible mace and whirling it again and again, he struck the arrogantly arrayed Mahāpārśva at the front of the battle.

sanskrit: sa svayā gadayā bhinno vikīrṇadaśanekṣaṇaḥ nipapāta mahāpārśvo vajrāhata ivācalaḥ
english: Mahāpārśva, cleaved by his own mace, his teeth and eyes scattered, fell like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tasmin hate bhrātari rāvaṇasya tan nairṛtānāṃ balam arṇavābham tyaktāyudhaṃ kevalajīvitārthaṃ dudrāva bhinnārṇavasaṃnikāśam
english: When that brother of Rāvaṇa was slain, that ocean-like Rākṣasa host, casting aside its weapons, fleeing with life as its only goal, scattered like a sea whose shores had been broken.

sanskrit: svabalaṃ vyathitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam bhrātṝṃś ca nihatān dṛṣṭvā śakratulyaparākramān
english: Seeing his own army in chaos and torment, hair-raising to behold, and seeing his brothers slain — those whose valour matched Indra's —

sanskrit: pitṛvyau cāpi saṃdṛśya samare saṃniṣūditau mahodaramahāpārśvau bhrātarau rākṣasarṣabhau
english: and beholding both his uncles cut down in battle — Mahodara and Mahāpārśva, those two bull-Rākṣasa brothers —

sanskrit: cukopa ca mahātejā brahmadattavaro yudhi atikāyo 'drisaṃkāśo devadānavadarpahā
english: the great-spirited Atikāya, who had received boons from Brahmā, mountain-like in form, crusher of the pride of gods and demons, blazed with fury in battle.

sanskrit: sa bhāskarasahasrasya saṃghātam iva bhāsvaram ratham āsthāya śakrārir abhidudrāva vānarān
english: Mounting his chariot blazing like a thousand suns together, Indra's foe rushed at the monkeys.

sanskrit: sa visphārya mahac cāpaṃ kirīṭī mṛṣṭakuṇḍalaḥ nāma viśrāvayām āsa nanāda ca mahāsvanam
english: Wearing his crown and gleaming earrings, he drew his great bow to its full span, proclaimed his name aloud, and roared with a mighty sound.

sanskrit: tena siṃhapraṇādena nāmaviśrāvaṇena ca jyāśabdena ca bhīmena trāsayām āsa vānarān
english: With that lion's roar, with the proclamation of his name, and with the fearsome twang of his bowstring, he struck terror into the monkeys.

sanskrit: te tasya rūpam ālokya yathā viṣṇos trivikrame bhayārtā vānarāḥ sarve vidravanti diśo daśa
english: Seeing his form, just as they might Viṣṇu in his three-stride stride, all the monkeys, seized by fear, scattered in the ten directions.

sanskrit: te 'tikāyaṃ samāsādya vānarā mūḍhacetasaḥ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmur lakṣmaṇāgrajam āhave
english: Those monkeys, their minds bewildered at the sight of Atikāya in battle, fled for refuge to the one worthy of refuge — the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: tato 'tikāyaṃ kākutstho rathasthaṃ parvatopamam dadarśa dhanvinaṃ dūrād garjantaṃ kālameghavat
english: Then Kākutstha (Rāma) beheld from afar Atikāya mounted in his chariot, mountain-like, bearing his bow, roaring like a storm cloud of Doomsday.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmānaṃ rāghavas tu suvismitaḥ vānarān sāntvayitvā tu vibhīṣaṇam uvāca ha
english: Seeing that great being, Rāghava was filled with wonder. Having calmed the monkeys, he addressed Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: ko 'sau parvatasaṃkāśo dhanuṣmān harilocanaḥ yukte hayasahasreṇa viśāle syandane sthitaḥ
english: "Who is that one, mountain-like, bearing a bow, with tawny eyes, standing in a vast chariot yoked with a thousand horses?

sanskrit: ya eṣa niśitaiḥ śūlaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiḥ prāsatomaraiḥ arciṣmadbhir vṛto bhāti bhūtair iva maheśvaraḥ
english: He who, surrounded by sharp spears, keen lances, and flaming javelins, shines like Maheśvara surrounded by supernatural beings —

sanskrit: kālajihvāprakāśābhir ya eṣo 'bhivirājate āvṛto rathaśaktībhir vidyudbhir iva toyadaḥ
english: who blazes forth, enveloped by chariot-spears gleaming like the tongues of Kāla, like a thundercloud enveloped by lightning?

sanskrit: dhanūṃsi cāsya sajyāni hemapṛṣṭhāni sarvaśaḥ śobhayanti rathaśreṣṭhaṃ śakrapātam ivāmbaram
english: His strung bows with golden backs adorn his excellent chariot on all sides, like Indra's bow adorns the sky.

sanskrit: ka eṣa rakṣaḥ śārdūlo raṇabhūmiṃ virājayan abhyeti rathināṃ śreṣṭho rathenādityatejasā
english: Who is this tiger among Rākṣasas who blazes upon the field of battle, advancing as the foremost of chariot warriors, with a chariot of solar splendour?

sanskrit: dhvajaśṛṅgapratiṣṭhena rāhuṇābhivirājate sūryaraśmiprabhair bāṇair diśo daśa virājayan
english: Rāhu set upon the peak of his standard blazes forth; with arrows bright as the rays of the sun he illumines the ten directions.

sanskrit: triṇataṃ meghanirhrādaṃ hemapṛṣṭham alaṃkṛtam śatakratudhanuḥprakhyaṃ dhanuś cāsya virājate
english: His bow, triply curved, its sound like the rumble of a thundercloud, its back adorned with gold, resplendent like the bow of Śatakratu (Indra), shines forth.

sanskrit: sadhvajaḥ sapatākaś ca sānukarṣo mahārathaḥ catuḥsādisamāyukto meghastanitanisvanaḥ
english: His great chariot bears a standard and pennant, has a dragging-pole, is yoked with four horses, and gives forth a sound like the roar of a thundercloud.

sanskrit: viṃśatir daśa cāṣṭau ca tūṇīraratham āsthitāḥ kārmukāṇi ca bhīmāni jyāś ca kāñcanapiṅgalāḥ
english: Thirty-eight quivers are ranged in the chariot; terrible bows and bowstrings tawny-gold are mounted there.

sanskrit: dvau ca khaḍgau rathagatau pārśvasthau pārśvaśobhinau caturhastatsarucitau vyaktahastadaśāyatau
english: Two swords in the chariot, placed at his flanks, adorning each side, fitted with hilts of four handbreadths, clearly ten handbreadths long.

sanskrit: raktakaṇṭhaguṇo dhīro mahāparvatasaṃnibhaḥ kālaḥ kālmahāvaktro meghastha iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Composed and resolute, wearing a crimson neck-cord, resembling a great mountain, like Kāla of mighty jaws — like the sun dwelling within a thundercloud.

sanskrit: kāñcanāṅgadanaddhābhyāṃ bhujābhyām eṣa śobhate śṛṅgābhyām iva tuṅgābhyāṃ himavān parvatottamaḥ
english: He is resplendent with his arms bound with golden armlets, like the great mountain Himavān with its two towering peaks.

sanskrit: kuṇḍalābhyāṃ tu yasyaitad bhāti vaktraṃ śubhekṣaṇam punarvasvantaragataṃ pūrṇabimbam ivaindavam
english: His face, with auspicious eyes and earrings, shines like the full disc of the moon stationed between the twin stars Punarvasu.

sanskrit: ācakṣva me mahābāho tvam enaṃ rākṣasottamam yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve bhayārtā vidrutā diśaḥ
english: O mighty-armed one, tell me who is this foremost of Rākṣasas — at whose sight all the monkeys, seized by fear, have fled in all directions?"

sanskrit: sa pṛṣṭho rājaputreṇa rāmeṇāmitatejasā ācacakṣe mahātejā rāghavāya vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Thus questioned by the royal prince Rāma of boundless splendour, the great-spirited Vibhīṣaṇa described him to Rāghava.

sanskrit: daśagrīvo mahātejā rājā vaiśravaṇānujaḥ bhīmakarmā mahotsāho rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: "The ten-necked one, great in splendour, king, younger brother of Vaiśravaṇa, terrible in his deeds, of enormous enterprise — Rāvaṇa, lord of Rākṣasas —

sanskrit: tasyāsīd vīryavān putro rāvaṇapratimo raṇe vṛddhasevī śrutadharaḥ sarvāstraviduṣāṃ varaḥ
english: had a mighty son, equal to Rāvaṇa in battle, respectful of elders, a retainer of sacred learning, foremost among all who know the science of weapons —

sanskrit: aśvapṛṣṭhe rathe nāge khaḍge dhanuṣi karṣaṇe bhede sāntve ca dāne ca naye mantre ca saṃmataḥ
english: honoured in the arts of horsemanship, chariot, elephant, sword, archery, in dissension, conciliation, giving, statecraft, and counsel —

sanskrit: yasya bāhuṃ samāśritya laṅkā bhavati nirbhayā tanayaṃ dhānyamālinyā atikāyam imaṃ viduḥ
english: relying on whose arm Laṅkā becomes fearless. This is Atikāya, known as the son of Dhānyamālinī.

sanskrit: etenārādhito brahmā tapasā bhāvitātmanā astrāṇi cāpy avāptāni ripavaś ca parājitāḥ
english: By him Brahmā was propitiated through austerity and a disciplined self; weapons too were obtained and enemies were vanquished.

sanskrit: surāsurair avadhyatvaṃ dattam asmai svayambhuvā etac ca kavacaṃ divyaṃ rathaś caiṣo 'rkabhāskaraḥ
english: The Self-born (Brahmā) granted him invulnerability before gods and demons; this divine armour and this chariot blazing like the sun were also given by him.

sanskrit: etena śataśo devā dānavāś ca parājitāḥ rakṣitāni ca rakṣāmi yakṣāś cāpi niṣūditāḥ
english: By him hundreds of gods and demons have been defeated; Rākṣasas have been protected, Yakṣas have been slaughtered.

sanskrit: vajraṃ viṣṭambhitaṃ yena bāṇair indrasya dhīmataḥ pāśaḥ salilarājasya yuddhe pratihatas tathā
english: By him the thunderbolt of the wise Indra was checked with arrows, and the noose of the lord of waters was repelled in battle.

sanskrit: eṣo 'tikāyo balavān rākṣasānām atharṣabhaḥ rāvaṇasya suto dhīmān devadanava darpahā
english: This is that powerful Atikāya, foremost bull among Rākṣasas, the wise son of Rāvaṇa, crusher of the pride of gods and demons.

sanskrit: tad asmin kriyatāṃ yatnaḥ kṣipraṃ puruṣapuṃgava purā vānarasainyāni kṣayaṃ nayati sāyakaiḥ
english: Therefore, O bull among men, let effort be made against him quickly, before he brings the monkey armies to destruction with his arrows."

sanskrit: tato 'tikāyo balavān praviśya harivāhinīm visphārayām āsa dhanur nanāda ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then powerful Atikāya, entering the monkey army, drew his bow taut and roared again and again.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmavapuṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathasthaṃ rathināṃ varam abhipetur mahātmāno ye pradhānāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: Seeing him of fearsome form standing in his chariot, the foremost of charioteers, those great-spirited monkeys who were the foremost leaders rushed against him.

sanskrit: kumudo dvivido maindo nīlaḥ śarabha eva ca pādapair giriśṛṅgaiś ca yugapat samabhidravan
english: Kumuda, Dvivida, Mainda, Nīla, and Śarabha charged together simultaneously with trees and mountain peaks.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vṛkṣāṃś ca śailāṃś ca śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇaiḥ atikāyo mahātejāś cicchedāstravidāṃ varaḥ
english: Those trees and mountains of theirs Atikāya, the great-spirited, foremost among those versed in weapons, cut to pieces with gold-ornamented arrows.

sanskrit: tāṃś caiva sarān sa harīñ śaraiḥ sarvāyasair balī vivyādhābhimukhaḥ saṃkhye bhīmakāyo niśācaraḥ
english: And those monkeys themselves, the mighty night-ranger of fearsome form, pierced with all-iron arrows as they advanced before him in battle.

sanskrit: te 'rditā bāṇabarṣeṇa bhinnagātrāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ na śekur atikāyasya pratikartuṃ mahāraṇe
english: Those monkeys, tormented by the shower of arrows, their bodies pierced, could not oppose Atikāya in the great battle.

sanskrit: tat sainyaṃ harivīrāṇāṃ trāsayām āsa rākṣasaḥ mṛgayūtham iva kruddho harir yauvanam āsthitaḥ
english: That Rākṣasa struck terror into the army of monkey heroes, as a lion in the prime of youth strikes terror into a herd of deer.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasendro harisainyamadhye nāyudhyamānaṃ nijaghāna kaṃ cit upetya rāmaṃ sadhanuḥ kalāpī sagarvitaṃ vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe
english: That lord of Rākṣasas, having not struck down anyone who stood unarmed in the monkey host, approached Rāma with bow and quiver and spoke this proud challenge.

sanskrit: rathe sthito 'haṃ śaracāpapāṇir na prākṛtaṃ kaṃ cana yodhayāmi yasyāsti śaktir vyavasāya yuktā dadātuṃ me kṣipram ihādya yuddham
english: "I stand in my chariot, arrows and bow in hand — I do not fight with ordinary men. Let him who has the strength and determination to give me swift battle today step forward now."

sanskrit: tat tasya vākyaṃ bruvato niśamya cukopa saumitrir amitrahantā amṛṣyamāṇaś ca samutpapāta jagrāha cāpaṃ ca tataḥ smayitvā
english: Hearing those words as he spoke them, Saumitri, slayer of foes, blazed with anger; refusing to endure it, he sprang forward, and then smiling, took up his bow.

sanskrit: kruddhaḥ saumitrir utpatya tūṇād ākṣipya sāyakam purastād atikāyasya vicakarṣa mahad dhanuḥ
english: Enraged, Saumitri leapt forward, drew an arrow from his quiver, and drew his great bow in front of Atikāya.

sanskrit: pūrayan sa mahīṃ śailān ākāśaṃ sāgaraṃ diśaḥ jyāśabdo lakṣmaṇasyogras trāsayan rajanīcarān
english: The fierce twang of Lakṣmaṇa's bowstring filled the earth, the mountains, the sky, the ocean, and all the directions, striking terror into the night-rangers.

sanskrit: saumitreś cāpanirghoṣaṃ śrutvā pratibhayaṃ tadā visiṣmiye mahātejā rākṣasendrātmajo balī
english: Hearing the fearsome crack of Saumitri's bow then, the mighty and powerful son of the lord of Rākṣasas was struck with wonder.

sanskrit: athātikāyaḥ kupito dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇam utthitam ādāya niśitaṃ bāṇam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Atikāya, angered at seeing Lakṣmaṇa step forward, took up a sharp arrow and spoke these words.

sanskrit: bālas tvam asi saumitre vikrameṣv avicakṣaṇaḥ gaccha kiṃ kālasadṛśaṃ māṃ yodhayitum icchasi
english: "You are a boy, O Saumitri, unskilled in feats of valour — go away. Why do you wish to fight me, who am like Death itself?

sanskrit: na hi madbāhusṛṣṭānām astrāṇāṃ himavān api soḍhum utsahate vegam antarikṣam atho mahī
english: Even Himavān cannot bear the speed of the weapons discharged from my arms, nor the sky, nor the earth.

sanskrit: sukhaprasuptaṃ kālāgniṃ prabodhayitum icchasi nyasya cāpaṃ nivartasva mā prāṇāñ jahi madgataḥ
english: You wish to rouse the fire of Doomsday from its easy sleep. Lay down your bow and turn back — do not lose your life by coming against me.

sanskrit: atha vā tvaṃ pratiṣṭabdho na nivartitum icchasi tiṣṭha prāṇān parityajya gamiṣyasi yamakṣayam
english: Or if you are so resolute you refuse to turn back — then stand, and abandoning your life, you shall go to the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: paśya me niśitān bāṇān aridarpaniṣūdanān īśvarāyudhasaṃkāśāṃs taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇān
english: Behold my sharp arrows, crushers of the enemy's pride, resembling the weapons of the Lord, adorned with heated gold.

sanskrit: eṣa te sarpasaṃkāśo bāṇaḥ pāsyati śoṇitam mṛgarāja iva kruddho nāgarājasya śoṇitam
english: This arrow of mine, like a serpent, shall drink your blood, as an enraged lion-king drinks the blood of the lord of elephants."

sanskrit: śrutvātikāyasya vacaḥ saroṣaṃ sagarvitaṃ saṃyati rājaputraḥ sa saṃcukopātibalo bṛhacchrīr uvāca vākyaṃ ca tato mahārtham
english: Hearing Atikāya's words, spoken in anger and pride in battle, that royal prince, the supremely powerful and greatly glorious one, blazed with fury and then spoke words of great import.

sanskrit: na vākyamātreṇa bhavān pradhāno na katthanāt satpuruṣā bhavanti mayi sthite dhanvini bāṇapāṇau vidarśayasvātmabalaṃ durātman
english: "One does not become eminent by words alone — good men are not made by boasting. With me standing here, bow in hand with arrow ready, show your own strength, O evil one!

sanskrit: karmaṇā sūcayātmānaṃ na vikatthitum arhasi pauruṣeṇa tu yo yuktaḥ sa tu śūra iti smṛtaḥ
english: Demonstrate yourself through deeds — you should not merely brag. He who is endowed with manliness is remembered as a hero.

sanskrit: sarvāyudhasamāyukto dhanvī tvaṃ ratham āsthitaḥ śarair vā yadi vāpy astrair darśayasva parākramam
english: Fully armed, a bowman, mounted in your chariot — show your prowess, whether with arrows or with supernatural weapons.

sanskrit: tataḥ śiras te niśitaiḥ pātayiṣyāmy ahaṃ śaraiḥ mārutaḥ kālasaṃpakvaṃ vṛntāt tālaphalaṃ yathā
english: Then I shall cut off your head with sharp arrows, as the wind fells a ripe palm-fruit from its stalk.

sanskrit: adya te māmakā bāṇās taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ pāsyanti rudhiraṃ gātrād bāṇaśalyāntarotthitam
english: Today my arrows, adorned with heated gold, shall drink blood gushing from your body among the arrow-tips.

sanskrit: bālo 'yam iti vijñāya na māvajñātum arhasi bālo vā yadi vā vṛddho mṛtyuṃ jānīhi saṃyuge
english: Knowing me to be a boy, you should not despise me. Whether boy or elder, know death in this battle."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā hetumat paramārthavat atikāyaḥ pracukrodha bāṇaṃ cottamam ādade
english: Hearing Lakṣmaṇa's words, reasoned and of supreme import, Atikāya blazed with fury and took up a supreme arrow.

sanskrit: tato vidyādharā bhūtā devā daityā maharṣayaḥ guhyakāś ca mahātmānas tad yuddhaṃ dadṛśus tadā
english: Then Vidyādharas, Bhūtas, gods, Daityas, great seers, and great-spirited Guhyakas all watched that battle.

sanskrit: tato 'tikāyaḥ kupitaś cāpam āropya sāyakam lakṣmaṇasya pracikṣepa saṃkṣipann iva cāmbaram
english: Then Atikāya, enraged, strung an arrow to his bow and shot it at Lakṣmaṇa, seeming to compress the very sky.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ niśitaṃ śaram āśīviṣopamam ardhacandreṇa ciccheda lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā
english: That sharp arrow like a venomous serpent as it came flying — Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, cut it with a crescent-headed arrow.

sanskrit: taṃ nikṛttaṃ śaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛttabhogam ivoragam atikāyo bhṛśaṃ kruddhaḥ pañcabāṇān samādade
english: Seeing that arrow cut down like a serpent whose hood had been severed, Atikāya, greatly enraged, took up five arrows.

sanskrit: tāñ śarān saṃpracikṣepa lakṣmaṇāya niśācaraḥ tān aprāptāñ śarais tīkṣṇaiś ciccheda bharatānujaḥ
english: Those arrows the night-ranger shot at Lakṣmaṇa; before they could arrive, the younger brother of Bharata cut them down with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: sa tāṃś chittvā śarais tīkṣṇair lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā ādade niśitaṃ bāṇaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā
english: Having cut those down with sharp arrows, Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, took up a sharp arrow blazing as if with energy.

sanskrit: tam ādāya dhanuḥ śreṣṭhe yojayām āsa lakṣmaṇaḥ vicakarṣa ca vegena visasarja ca sāyakam
english: Taking it and fitting it to his excellent bow, Lakṣmaṇa drew it swiftly and released the arrow.

sanskrit: pūrṇāyatavisṛṣṭena śareṇānata parvaṇā lalāṭe rākṣasaśreṣṭham ājaghāna sa vīryavān
english: With that arrow released at full draw, its joints smooth, that valorous one struck the foremost of Rākṣasas on the forehead.

sanskrit: sa lalāṭe śaro magnas tasya bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ dadṛśe śoṇitenāktaḥ pannagendra ivāhave
english: The arrow, sunk into the forehead of that fearsome Rākṣasa, was seen red with blood in battle, like the lord of serpents.

sanskrit: rākṣasaḥ pracakampe ca lakṣmaṇeṣu prakampitaḥ rudrabāṇahataṃ bhīmaṃ yathā tripuragopuram
english: The Rākṣasa shook, struck by Lakṣmaṇa's arrows, as the terrible gate-tower of Tripura shook when struck by Rudra's arrow.

sanskrit: cintayām āsa cāśvasya vimṛśya ca mahābalaḥ sādhu bāṇanipātena śvāghanīyo 'si me ripuḥ
english: Recovering himself, the mighty one reflected and thought: "By this fall of arrows you are truly a foe worthy of being slain tomorrow."

sanskrit: vicāryaivaṃ vinamyāsyaṃ vinamya ca bhujāv ubhau sa rathopastham āsthāya rathena pracacāra ha
english: Having considered thus, he bent his head, bowed both his arms, and taking his stance on the chariot-platform, maneuvered with his chariot.

sanskrit: ekaṃ trīn pañca sapteti sāyakān rākṣasarṣabhaḥ ādade saṃdadhe cāpi vicakarṣotsasarja ca
english: One, three, five, seven — arrows the bull among Rākṣasas took up, fitted, drew to the full, and discharged.

sanskrit: te bāṇāḥ kālasaṃkāśā rākṣasendradhanuś cyutāḥ hemapuṅkhā raviprakhyāś cakrur dīptam ivāmbaram
english: Those arrows, like Death himself, discharged from the bow of the lord of Rākṣasas, with golden fletching, bright as the sun, made the sky blaze as if on fire.

sanskrit: tatas tān rākṣasotsṛṣṭāñ śaraughān rāvaṇānujaḥ asaṃbhrāntaḥ praciccheda niśitair bahubhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Rāvaṇa's younger brother (Lakṣmaṇa), unperturbed, cut down those streams of arrows released by the Rākṣasa with many sharp arrows of his own.

sanskrit: tāñ śarān yudhi saṃprekṣya nikṛttān rāvaṇātmajaḥ cukopa tridaśendrārir jagrāha niśitaṃ śaram
english: Seeing those arrows cut down in battle, the son of Rāvaṇa, foe of the lord of the thirty gods, blazed with fury and seized a sharp arrow.

sanskrit: sa saṃdhāya mahātejās taṃ bāṇaṃ sahasotsṛjat tataḥ saumitrim āyāntam ājaghāna stanāntare
english: The great-spirited one, fitting that arrow, suddenly released it; he struck Saumitri then in the chest as he came forward.

sanskrit: atikāyena saumitris tāḍito yudhi vakṣasi susrāva rudhiraṃ tīvraṃ madaṃ matta iva dvipaḥ
english: Struck by Atikāya in battle on the chest, Saumitri poured forth copious blood, like a rutting elephant in rut.

sanskrit: sa cakāra tadātmānaṃ viśalyaṃ sahasā vibhuḥ jagrāha ca śaraṃ tīṣṇam astreṇāpi samādadhe
english: That mighty one instantly extracted the arrow from himself, took up a keen arrow, and charged it with a supernatural weapon.

sanskrit: āgneyena tadāstreṇa yojayām āsa sāyakam sa jajvāla tadā bāṇo dhanuś cāsya mahātmanaḥ
english: He charged that arrow with the Āgneya weapon of fire; the arrow then blazed, and so did the bow of that great-spirited one.

sanskrit: atikāyo 'titejasvī sauram astraṃ samādade tena bāṇaṃ bhujaṃgābhaṃ hemapuṅkham ayojayat
english: The supremely brilliant Atikāya charged the Saura weapon of the sun, and with it fitted an arrow like a serpent with golden fletching.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ jvalitaṃ ghoraṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ śaram āhitam atikāyāya cikṣepa kāladaṇḍam ivāntakaḥ
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa hurled that blazing, terrible charged arrow at Atikāya, like Death hurling his rod of Kāla.

sanskrit: āgneyenābhisaṃyuktaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāṇaṃ niśācaraḥ utsasarja tadā bāṇaṃ dīptaṃ sūryāstrayojitam
english: Seeing the arrow charged with the Āgneya weapon coming at him, the night-ranger discharged his own blazing arrow charged with the Saura solar weapon.

sanskrit: tāv ubhāv ambare bāṇāv anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ tejasā saṃpradīptāgrau kruddhāv iva bhujaṃgamau
english: Those two arrows in the sky struck each other, their tips blazing with energy, like two enraged serpents.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ vinirdahya petatur dharaṇītale nirarciṣau bhasmakṛtau na bhrājete śarottamau
english: Having consumed each other mutually, those two supreme arrows fell to the surface of the earth, reduced to ash, without flame, their glory extinguished.

sanskrit: tato 'tikāyaḥ saṃkruddhas tv astram aiṣīkam utsṛjat tat praciccheda saumitrir astram aindreṇa vīryavān
english: Then Atikāya, greatly enraged, discharged the Aiṣīka reed-weapon; the valorous Saumitri cut it down with the Aindra weapon of Indra.

sanskrit: aiṣīkaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā kumāro rāvaṇātmajaḥ yāmyenāstreṇa saṃkruddho yojayām āsa sāyakam
english: Seeing the Aiṣīka weapon destroyed, that young son of Rāvaṇa, greatly enraged, charged an arrow with the Yāmya weapon of Yama.

sanskrit: tatas tad astraṃ cikṣepa lakṣmaṇāya niśācaraḥ vāyavyena tad astraṃ tu nijaghāna sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: The night-ranger then hurled that weapon at Lakṣmaṇa; but Lakṣmaṇa destroyed that weapon with the Vāyavya weapon of Vāyu.

sanskrit: athainaṃ śaradhārābhir dhārābhir iva toyadaḥ abhyavarṣata saṃkruddho lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇātmajam
english: Then enraged Lakṣmaṇa showered the son of Rāvaṇa with streams of arrows like a thundercloud showering streams of rain.

sanskrit: te 'tikāyaṃ samāsādya kavace vajrabhūṣite bhagnāgraśalyāḥ sahasā petur bāṇā mahītale
english: Those arrows, reaching Atikāya's armour adorned with diamond-hard metal, instantly fell to the ground with their tips and shafts broken.

sanskrit: tān moghān abhisaṃprekṣya lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā abhyavarṣata bāṇānāṃ sahasreṇa mahāyaśāḥ
english: Seeing those arrows made fruitless, Lakṣmaṇa the slayer of enemy heroes, of great fame, showered him with thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: sa varṣyamāṇo bāṇaughair atikāyo mahābalaḥ avadhyakavacaḥ saṃkhye rākṣaso naiva vivyathe
english: Even drenched with streams of arrows, Atikāya the mighty Rākṣasa, shielded by his impenetrable armour, did not even flinch in battle.

sanskrit: na śaśāka rujaṃ kartuṃ yudhi tasya narottamaḥ athainam abhyupāgamya vāyur vākyam uvāca ha
english: That foremost of men could not inflict a wound upon him in battle. Then the Wind-god himself approached and spoke to him.

sanskrit: brahmadattavaro hy eṣa avadhya kavacāvṛtaḥ brāhmeṇāstreṇa bhindhy enam eṣa vadhyo hi nānyathā
english: "He has received a boon from Brahmā and is protected by impenetrable armour. Pierce him with the Brahmā weapon — he can be slain by no other means."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vāyor vacanaṃ niśamya saumitrir indrapratimānavīryaḥ samādade bāṇam amoghavegaṃ tad brāhmam astraṃ sahasā niyojya
english: Then Saumitri, whose valour matches Indra's, hearing the words of Vāyu, instantly took up an arrow of unfailing speed and charged it at once with that Brahmā weapon.

sanskrit: tasmin varāstre tu niyujyamāne saumitriṇā bāṇavare śitāgre diśaḥ sacandrārkamahāgrahāś ca nabhaś ca tatrāsa rarāsa corvī
english: As that supreme weapon was being charged by Saumitri onto his best arrow with sharp tip, the directions with moon, sun, and great planets, the sky itself, trembled and roared, and the earth shook.

sanskrit: taṃ brahmaṇo 'streṇa niyujya cāpe śaraṃ supuṅkhaṃ yamadūtakalpam saumitrir indrārisutasya tasya sasarja bāṇaṃ yudhi vajrakalpam
english: Lakṣmaṇa charged that well-fletched arrow, the equal of Yama's messenger, with Brahmā's weapon on his bow and discharged it in battle at the son of Indra's foe — an arrow like a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: taṃ lakṣmaṇotsṛṣṭam amoghavegaṃ samāpatantaṃ jvalanaprakāśam suvarṇavajrottamacitrapuṅkhaṃ tadātikāyaḥ samare dadarśa
english: That arrow discharged by Lakṣmaṇa, of unfailing speed, as it came flying, bright as fire, with fine golden and diamond-decorated fletching — Atikāya then beheld it in battle.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣamāṇaḥ sahasātikāyo jaghāna bāṇair niśitair anekaiḥ sa sāyakas tasya suparṇavegas tadātivegena jagāma pārśvam
english: Even as Atikāya was watching it, he instantly struck it with many sharp arrows; yet that arrow, swift as Garuḍa, came to his side with yet greater speed.

sanskrit: tam āgataṃ prekṣya tadātikāyo bāṇaṃ pradīptāntakakālakalpam jaghāna śaktyṛṣṭigadākuṭhāraiḥ śūlair halaiś cāpy avipannaceṣṭaḥ
english: Seeing that arrow come — like blazing Death and Kāla combined — Atikāya struck at it with spears, iron darts, maces, axes, pikes, and ploughs, his efforts unimpeded.

sanskrit: tāny āyudhāny adbhutavigrahāṇi moghāni kṛtvā sa śaro 'gnidīptaḥ prasahya tasyaiva kirīṭajuṣṭaṃ tadātikāyasya śiro jahāra
english: Making all those weapons of wondrous form futile, that arrow blazing with fire forcefully took off Atikāya's head adorned with its crown then and there.

sanskrit: tac chiraḥ saśiras trāṇaṃ lakṣmaṇeṣuprapīḍitam papāta sahasā bhūmau śṛṅgaṃ himavato yathā
english: That head together with its helmet-armour, driven by Lakṣmaṇa's arrow, fell suddenly to the earth like a peak of Himavān.

sanskrit: praharṣayuktā bahavas tu vānarā prabuddhapadmapratimānanās tadā apūjayaṃl lakṣmaṇam iṣṭabhāginaṃ hate ripau bhīmabale durāsade
english: Then many monkeys, filled with great joy, their faces like blossomed lotuses, honoured Lakṣmaṇa, the fortunate one, upon the slaying of that fearsome, formidable foe.

sanskrit: tato hatān rākṣasapuṃgavāṃs tān devāntakāditriśiro 'tikāyān rakṣogaṇās tatra hatāvaśiṣṭās te rāvaṇāya tvaritaṃ śaśaṃsuḥ
english: Then the surviving Rākṣasa bands there, those who remained after the slaughter, swiftly reported to Rāvaṇa the killing of those bull-Rākṣasas — Devāntaka, Triśiras, Atikāya, and the rest.

sanskrit: tato hatāṃs tān sahasā niśamya rājā mumohāśrupariplutākṣaḥ putrakṣayaṃ bhrātṛvadhaṃ ca ghoraṃ vicintya rājā vipulaṃ pradadhyau
english: Then the king, hearing at once of those who were slain, fell into a swoon, his eyes flooded with tears; pondering the destruction of his sons and the terrible killing of his brothers, the king brooded deeply.

sanskrit: tatas tu rājānam udīkṣya dīnaṃ śokārṇave saṃparipupluvānam atharṣabho rākṣasarājasūnur athendrajid vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe
english: Then seeing the king so wretched, tossed in the ocean of grief, that bull among the sons of the king of Rākṣasas — Indrajit — spoke these words.

sanskrit: na tāta mohaṃ pratigantum arhasi yatrendrajij jīvati rākṣasendra nendrāribāṇābhihato hi kaś cit prāṇān samarthaḥ samare 'bhidhartum
english: "O father, you should not fall into bewilderment while Indrajit yet lives, O lord of Rākṣasas — no one struck by the arrows of Indra's foe is capable of preserving his life in battle.

sanskrit: paśyādya rāmaṃ sahalakṣmaṇena madbāṇanirbhinnavikīrṇadeham gatāyuṣaṃ bhūmitale śayānaṃ śaraiḥ śitair ācitasarvagātram
english: See today Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa, their bodies pierced and shattered by my arrows, lying on the ground deprived of life, their every limb covered with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: imāṃ pratijñāṃ śṛṇu śakraśatroḥ suniścitāṃ pauruṣadaivayuktām adyaiva rāmaṃ sahalakṣmaṇena saṃtāpayiṣyāmi śarair amoghaiḥ
english: Hear this vow of Indra's foe, firmly resolved and joined with manly power and destiny: this very day I shall torment Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa with unfailing arrows.

sanskrit: adyendravaivasvataviṣṇumitra sādhyāśvivaiśvānaracandrasūryāḥ drakṣyanti me vikramam aprameyaṃ viṣṇor ivograṃ baliyajñavāṭe
english: Today Indra, Vivasvat's son (Yama), Viṣṇu, Mitra, the Sādhyas, the Aśvins, Vaiśvānara, Moon, and Sun shall see my immeasurable valour, fierce as Viṣṇu's at the sacrificial grounds of Bali."

sanskrit: sa evam uktvā tridaśendraśatrur āpṛcchya rājānam adīnasattvaḥ samārurohānilatulyavegaṃ rathaṃ kharaśreṣṭhasamādhiyuktam
english: Having spoken thus, Indra's foe, undaunted in spirit, took leave of the king and mounted his chariot swift as the wind, equipped with the finest mules.

sanskrit: samāsthāya mahātejā rathaṃ harirathopamam jagāma sahasā tatra yatra yuddham ariṃdama
english: The great-spirited one, mounting his chariot rivalling Hari's own, swiftly went to where the battle was, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: taṃ prasthitaṃ mahātmānam anujagmur mahābalāḥ saṃharṣamāṇā bahavo dhanuḥpravarapāṇayaḥ
english: Many mighty warriors, exulting, followed that great-souled one as he set forth, their hands holding excellent bows.

sanskrit: gajaskandhagatāḥ ke cit ke cit paramavājibhiḥ prāsamudgaranistriṃśa paraśvadhagadādharāḥ
english: Some were mounted on the backs of elephants, some on the finest horses, bearing lances, hammers, swords, axes, and maces.

sanskrit: sa śaṅkhaninadair bhīmair bherīṇāṃ ca mahāsvanaiḥ jagāma tridaśendrāriḥ stūyamāno niśācaraiḥ
english: With fearsome blasts of conch-shells and the great roar of kettledrums, Indra's foe advanced, praised by the night-rangers.

sanskrit: sa śaṅkhaśaśivarṇena chatreṇa ripusādanaḥ rarāja paripūrṇena nabhaś candramasā yathā
english: That slayer of foes blazed resplendent beneath a parasol white as the conch or the moon, like the sky with the full moon.

sanskrit: avījyata tato vīro haimair hemavibhūṣitaiḥ cārucāmaramukhyaiḥ ca mukhyaḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām
english: Then that hero, foremost among all bowmen, was fanned with golden fly-whisks adorned with gold, with beautiful tufts of yak-tail.

sanskrit: tatas tv indrajitā laṅkā sūryapratimatejasā rarājāprativīryeṇa dyaur ivārkeṇa bhāsvatā
english: Then Laṅkā with Indrajit, whose energy rivals the sun, whose valour is unmatched, blazed resplendent as the sky with the shining sun.

sanskrit: sa tu dṛṣṭvā viniryāntaṃ balena mahatā vṛtam rākṣasādhipatiḥ śrīmān rāvaṇaḥ putram abravīt
english: Seeing him going forth surrounded by a great army, the glorious lord of Rākṣasas Rāvaṇa spoke to his son.

sanskrit: tvam apratirathaḥ putra jitas te yudhi vāsavaḥ kiṃ punar mānuṣaṃ dhṛṣyaṃ na vadhiṣyasi rāghavam
english: "You are a warrior without a match in chariot-battle, my son; you have conquered Vāsava (Indra) in battle. Why would you not slay the audacious human Rāghava?"

sanskrit: tathokto rākṣasendreṇa pratigṛhya mahāśiṣaḥ rathenāśvayujā vīraḥ śīghraṃ gatvā nikumbhilām
english: Thus addressed by the lord of Rākṣasas, the hero received his great blessings, and going swiftly with his horse-yoked chariot to Nikumbhilā —

sanskrit: sa saṃprāpya mahātejā yuddhabhūmim ariṃdamaḥ sthāpayām āsa rakṣāṃsi rathaṃ prati samantataḥ
english: that great-spirited subduer of foes, having reached the sacred battle-ground, stationed Rākṣasas all around the chariot as guard.

sanskrit: tatas tu hutabhoktāraṃ hutabhuk sadṛśaprabhaḥ juhuve rākṣasaśreṣṭho mantravad vidhivat tadā
english: Then that foremost of Rākṣasas, whose lustre equals fire, invoked the consumer of oblations — fire — with sacred mantras and proper ritual.

sanskrit: sa havirjālasaṃskārair mālyagandhapuraskṛtaiḥ juhuve pāvakaṃ tatra rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān
english: That mighty lord of Rākṣasas, with the rites of a network of oblations, preceded by garlands and fragrant substances, poured libations into the fire there.

sanskrit: śastrāṇi śarapatrāṇi samidho 'tha vibhītakaḥ lohitāni ca vāsāṃsi sruvaṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ tathā
english: Weapons, arrow-feathers, and kindling-sticks of vibhītaka wood, garments dyed red, and a ladle of black iron were offered.

sanskrit: sa tatrāgniṃ samāstīrya śarapatraiḥ satomaraiḥ chāgasya sarvakṛṣṇasya galaṃ jagrāha jīvataḥ
english: Having spread the fire there with arrow-feathers and javelins, he grasped the throat of an all-black living goat.

sanskrit: sakṛd eva samiddhasya vidhūmasya mahārciṣaḥ babhūvus tāni liṅgāni vijayaṃ yāny adarśayan
english: Even as the fire was kindled just once, smokeless and blazing high with great flames, those omens appeared which foretold victory.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇāvartaśikhas taptakāñcanasaṃnibhaḥ havis tat pratijagrāha pāvakaḥ svayam utthitaḥ
english: With its flames turning clockwise, resembling heated gold, fire itself rose up and accepted those oblations.

sanskrit: so 'stram āhārayām āsa brāhmam astravidāṃ varaḥ dhanuś cātmarathaṃ caiva sarvaṃ tatrābhyamantrayat
english: He, foremost among those versed in weapons, summoned the Brahmā weapon and consecrated his bow, his chariot, and all his armaments with sacred mantras there.

sanskrit: tasminn āhūyamāne 'stre hūyamāne ca pāvake sārkagrahendu nakṣatraṃ vitatrāsa nabhastalam
english: As that weapon was being invoked and as the fire was being fed with oblations, the sky together with sun, planets, moon, and stars trembled with fear.

sanskrit: sa pāvakaṃ pāvakadīptatejā hutvā mahendrapratimaprabhāvaḥ sacāpabāṇāsirathāśvasūtaḥ khe 'ntardadha ātmānam acintyarūpaḥ
english: Having made oblation into the fire, he whose energy blazes like fire, whose power rivals great Indra's, bearing bow, arrows, sword, chariot, horses, and charioteer, concealed himself in the sky — he of inconceivable form.

sanskrit: sa sainyam utsṛjya sametya tūrṇaṃ mahāraṇe vānaravāhinīṣu adṛśyamānaḥ śarajālam ugraṃ vavarṣa nīlāmbudharo yathāmbu
english: Leaving his army behind and swiftly entering the monkey armies in the great battle while remaining invisible, he rained down a fierce web of arrows, as a dark rain-cloud rains water.

sanskrit: te śakrajidbāṇaviśīrṇadehā māyāhatā visvaram unnadantaḥ raṇe nipetur harayo 'drikalpā yathendravajrābhihatā nagendrāḥ
english: Those monkeys, mountain-like, their bodies shattered by the arrows of Indra's conqueror, struck down by māyā, crying out in discordant voices, fell in battle like great elephants struck by Indra's thunderbolt.

sanskrit: te kevalaṃ saṃdadṛśuḥ śitāgrān bāṇān raṇe vānaravāhinīṣu māyā nigūḍhaṃ ca surendraśatruṃ na cātra taṃ rākṣasam abhyapaśyan
english: They saw only the sharp-tipped arrows in the monkey armies in battle; they could not see the foe of the lord of gods, hidden by māyā — they did not perceive that Rākṣasa there at all.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rakṣo'dhipatir mahātmā sarvā diśo bāṇagaṇaiḥ śitāgraiḥ pracchādayām āsa raviprakāśair viṣādayām āsa ca vānarendrān
english: Then that great-souled lord of Rākṣasas covered all the directions with swarms of sharp-tipped arrows bright as the sun and filled the lords of monkeys with despair.

sanskrit: sa śūlanistriṃśa paraśvadhāni vyāvidhya dīptānalasaṃnibhāni savisphuliṅgojjvalapāvakāni vavarṣa tīvraṃ plavagendrasainye
english: He whirled and rained down fiercely upon the army of monkey lords — spears, swords, and battle-axes resembling blazing fire, blazing with flames and sparks.

sanskrit: tato jvalanasaṃkāśaiḥ śitair vānarayūthapāḥ tāḍitāḥ śakrajidbāṇaiḥ praphullā iva kiṃśukāḥ
english: Then the leaders of the monkey troops, struck by the arrows of Indra's conqueror, blazing like fire, bloomed like kimśuka flowers in full bloom.

sanskrit: anyonyam abhisarpanto ninadantaś ca visvaram rākṣasendrāstranirbhinnā nipetur vānararṣabhāḥ
english: Crawling toward one another and crying out in discordant voices, bull-monkeys pierced by the weapons of the lord of Rākṣasas fell down.

sanskrit: udīkṣamāṇā gaganaṃ ke cin netreṣu tāḍitāḥ śarair viviśur anyonyaṃ petuś ca jagatītale
english: Some gazing up at the sky were struck in the eyes; pierced by arrows they collapsed into one another and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: hanūmantaṃ ca sugrīvam aṅgadaṃ gandhamādanam jāmbavantaṃ suṣeṇaṃ ca vegadarśinam eva ca
english: Hanūmān, Sugrīva, Aṅgada, Gandhamādana, Jāmbavān, Suṣeṇa, and Vegadarśin —

sanskrit: maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ nīlaṃ gavākṣaṃ gajagomukhau kesariṃ harilomānaṃ vidyuddaṃṣṭraṃ ca vānaram
english: Mainda, Dvivida, Nīla, Gavākṣa, Gaja, Gomukha, Keśarin, Hariloman, and the monkey Vidyuddaṃṣṭra —

sanskrit: sūryānanaṃ jyotimukhaṃ tathā dadhimukhaṃ harim pāvakākṣaṃ nalaṃ caiva kumudaṃ caiva vānaram
english: Sūryānana, Jyotimukha, Dadhimukha the monkey, Pāvakākṣa, Nala, and the monkey Kumuda —

sanskrit: prāsaiḥ śūlaiḥ śitair bāṇair indrajinmantrasaṃhitaiḥ vivyādha hariśārdūlān sarvāṃs tān rākṣasottamaḥ
english: — all these tiger-monkeys that foremost of Rākṣasas pierced with lances, pikes, and sharp arrows charged with Indrajit's mantras.

sanskrit: sa vai gadābhir hariyūthamukhyān nirbhidya bāṇais tapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ vavarṣa rāmaṃ śaravṛṣṭijālaiḥ salakṣmaṇaṃ bhāskararaśmikalpaiḥ
english: Having shattered the monkey troop-leaders with maces and pierced them with gold-fletched arrows, he rained webs of arrow-showers upon Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa — arrows like the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: sa bāṇavarṣair abhivarṣyamāṇo dhārānipātān iva tān vicintya samīkṣamāṇaḥ paramādbhutaśrī rāmas tadā lakṣmaṇam ity uvāca
english: Drenched in those showers of arrows, reflecting on them as if they were streams of falling rain, Rāma of supremely wondrous glory, surveying all around him, then spoke to Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: asau punar lakṣmaṇa rākṣasendro brahmāstram āśritya surendraśatruḥ nipātayitvā harisainyam ugram asmāñ śarair ardayati prasaktam
english: "This lord of Rākṣasas again, O Lakṣmaṇa — Indra's foe — having felled the fierce monkey army, relying on the Brahmā weapon, torments us continually with his arrows.

sanskrit: svayambhuvā dattavaro mahātmā kham āsthito 'ntarhitabhīmakāyaḥ kathaṃ nu śakyo yudhi naṣṭadeho nihantum adyendrajid udyatāstraḥ
english: He is great-souled, bearing a boon from the Self-born, stationed in the sky with his fearsome body concealed — how then can Indrajit, invisible in form and weapons raised, be killed today in battle?

sanskrit: manye svayambhūr bhagavān acintyo yasyaitad astraṃ prabhavaś ca yo 'sya bāṇāvapātāṃs tvam ihādya dhīman mayā sahāvyagramanāḥ sahasva
english: I think the blessed Self-born, who is inconceivable, is the source of this weapon and of him who wields it. You, O wise one, endure here with me today without anxiety the falls of his arrows.

sanskrit: pracchādayaty eṣa hi rākṣasendraḥ sarvā diśaḥ sāyakavṛṣṭijālaiḥ etac ca sarvaṃ patitāgryavīraṃ na bhrājate vānararājasainyam
english: For this lord of Rākṣasas covers all the directions with webs of arrow-showers; and this entire army of the monkey king no longer shines, its foremost heroes having fallen.

sanskrit: āvāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā patitau visaṃjñau nivṛttayuddhau hataroṣaharṣau dhruvaṃ pravekṣyaty amarārivāsaṃ asau samādāya raṇāgralakṣmīm
english: And seeing the two of us fallen and senseless, withdrawn from battle, our fury and joy extinguished, he will surely enter the abode of the enemies of the immortals, having taken away the glory of the battle's vanguard.

sanskrit: tatas tu tāv indrajid astrajālair babhūvatus tatra tadā viśastau sa cāpi tau tatra viṣādayitvā nanāda harṣād yudhi rākṣasendraḥ
english: Then those two were there struck down and rendered helpless by Indrajit's web of weapons; and having brought them to despair there, the lord of Rākṣasas roared with joy in battle.

sanskrit: sa tat tadā vānararājasainyaṃ rāmaṃ ca saṃkhye sahalakṣmaṇena viṣādayitvā sahasā viveśa purīṃ daśagrīvabhujābhiguptām
english: Having thus brought the army of the monkey king and Rāma together with Lakṣmaṇa to despair in battle, he swiftly entered the city protected by the arms of the ten-necked one.
